Tiny – Help

Tiny 0.13.1 · 29.10.2026

Start and camera selection

Open start.sh or the Tiny launcher. Live view starts automatically after discovery. Choose Tiny 2 or Logitech C922 at the top; preview switches automatically. Tiny 2 is woken and its status checked before starting video. Pass the camera through to the VM where applicable. Camera selection is locked during recording.

Live view and errors

Connecting live view remains visible until the first frame arrives, followed by Live view running. Camera → Stop live view stops it; Camera → Start live view restarts it. F5 rediscovers devices when preview is stopped and restarts the selected camera. Check USB, other camera apps and the log on errors.

Controls

Movement & zoom, Tracking, Image & focus, Presets and Camera settings are available in the sidebar. They provide Tiny controls, subject tracking, image controls and saved camera positions; available UVC controls depend on the camera driver. Diagnostics remains hidden. Image format, Video, Audio, Camera profiles and virtual-camera output are also available. Video contains camera resolution, frame rate and pixel format, plus recording format, quality, bitrate, rotation, filters and recording duration.

Mirroring

Camera → Mirror horizontally applies to live view, PNG and video. The choice is saved and also appears in Settings. Pixel aiming uses the current unmodified preview and compensates for mirroring. Mirror changes are locked during recording.

Recording and camera microphone

Capture → Save snapshot writes PNG (Ctrl+S). Capture → Record video writes WebM (Ctrl+R); Finish recording closes it (Ctrl+Shift+R). With audio enabled, recording always uses a microphone belonging to the selected camera, matched through its physical USB parent. There is no separate microphone selector. Missing or muted camera inputs produce an error; no other microphone is substituted. Record audio can be explicitly disabled. Existing files are protected. Closing finishes an active recording first. Camera media is not uploaded.

Image format

Select a format reported by the camera. Choose an available format: PNG, JPEG, BMP, ICO/CUR, TIFF or WebP, then click Save image. The Audio page also provides separate microphone recording with its own destination folder and locally available audio formats. Video recordings can include audio as well: Opus (WebM/MKV), AAC (MP4) or PCM (AVI), depending on installed encoders.

Formats and limits

Tested: C922 at 1080p/30 and 720p/30 or 60; Tiny 2 at 720p/30. File → Settings sets width and frame rate for the next preview start. C922 has no motorized gimbal or OBSBOT tracking. Tiny 2 position reads on Linux may report the last target; speed movement and roll are unavailable. Tracking can override manual movement.

Language and voice commands

File → Settings offers ten interface languages and local language pack import. Language changes update the interface and responses immediately. This application has no speech recognizer yet. The camera-internal Tiny 2 voice control supports English and Mandarin according to its manufacturer, with no German language setting. German software voice commands would require a separate extension.

Help and diagnostics

F1 and Help → Help open this local guide. Help → About shows dependencies and contributors; Help → Logs opens the bounded local logs. The separate diagnostics page has been removed from this interface.

Video format and camera controls

Use the Video format page to select a resolution, frame rate and pixel format reported by the camera. Changing formats restarts the preview. The display separates negotiated and measured frame rates. A separate camera-controls page is not available in this interface.

Capture

Use Image format to save photos. The Video page starts and stops recordings and asks for the save location. Video contains camera resolution, frame rate and pixel format, plus container, quality, bitrate, rotation, recording duration and filters. Audio uses the selected USB camera microphone. Crosshair and watermark remain display-only.

Camera profiles

Enter a profile name and click Save. To restore a profile, select it and click Load. Profiles include video format and frame rate, recording format and options, rotation, grayscale, negative, mirroring, crosshair and valid camera image controls. They are stored locally per camera in camera_profiles.json. Tiny pan/tilt and virtual-camera output are not stored. To remove a profile, select it and click Delete.

Extras → Restore driver defaults resets valid controls after confirmation. Invalid driver values and individual Tiny movement controls are excluded. This is not a manufacturer factory reset.

Closing

Closing finalizes recordings and puts Tiny cameras used by this application to sleep, even after switching to Logitech. Failure to confirm sleep is reported.

Other cameras and errors

Other V4L2 cameras are detected from their capture capabilities. Support depends on the device, Linux driver and codecs. F5 refreshes the device list while preview is stopped. A VM requires explicit USB passthrough. The diagnostics page has been removed; logs remain available from Help → Logs.

Virtual camera

Select a configured output device and video format under Virtual camera. Use Extras → Virtual camera to start or stop forwarding. Image filters are included; display overlays are excluded. Only physical sources can be forwarded, to prevent feedback loops. A separately configured akvcam or v4l2loopback driver is required. The configuration example can be saved without applying it. Only video is forwarded; use the physical camera’s microphone in the receiving application.

Voice/Gestures

The sidebar page contains Voice and Gestures tabs. Every command and gesture has its own visible row and independently saved switch. Voice also contains the recognition language (English/Chinese). Select a row, set its value and click Apply. Only the highlighted row in the active tab is sent. Changing a switch automatically highlights its row. Please check the effect on the camera.

Hand signs: open palm for tracking; thumb and index finger forming an L for zoom; two L-shaped hands for dynamic zoom, then change their distance. Reversing zoom direction uses the same two-hand gesture. Keep hands beside your face.

Capture quality and failure handling

JPEG image quality is saved separately and applies to single photos and series. Other image formats disable this control. Photo series use the selected image format. MP4/H.264 quality is controlled by bitrate. Recording and profile saving are disabled without video encoders. Failed audio finalization preserves the file and reports its location. Unreliable driver controls are read-only; use Image & Focus for Tiny 2 exposure.
